title: Andy's Mind: A Co-created Serious Game for People With Psychosis (PSICOGAME)
official: Development and Evaluation of the Effectiveness of a Psychoeducational Serious Game for People With Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether Andy's Mind, a psychoeducational card game co-created with a person with lived experience of psychosis, improves illness awareness (insight) and attitudes toward treatment in adults with schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders, compared with conventional group psychoeducation.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Andy's Mind improve insight into mental disorder more than conventional psychoeducation?
* Does Andy's Mind improve attitudes toward medication, as an indicator of treatment adherence, more than conventional psychoeducation?

Researchers will also look at psychotic symptoms, attitudes toward alcohol and other drugs, and participant satisfaction.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of two groups: the Andy's Mind game group or a conventional psychoeducation group.
* Attend 8 weekly group sessions of 45 minutes. Both groups cover the same topics: what psychosis is, symptoms, treatment, side effects, substance use and relapse prevention.
* Complete interviews and questionnaires before the sessions, right after the last session, and two months later.

The study takes place in mental health services in Catalonia, Spain, including prison mental health units, psychosocial rehabilitation services and community mental health centers.
conditions: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 65 years, inclusive.
* Diagnosis within the schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders according to DSM-5: schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, delusional disorder, brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, substance/medication-induced psychotic disorder, psychotic disorder due to another medical condition, or unspecified psychotic disorder.
* Receiving care in a prison, community or rehabilitation mental health service.
* Signed informed consent from the participant and, when applicable, from the legal guardian.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Moderate or severe intellectual disability.
* Cognitive impairment on the Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry, Spanish version (SCIP-S), defined as a total score below the 5th percentile or any subscale score below the 3rd percentile according to clinical-sample norms adjusted for age and educational level.
* Active psychotic episode.
* Language barrier preventing completion of the assessments or participation in the group sessions.
* Previous participation in the Phase 1 usability pilot of the study.
